title: Ninja dynamic-dependency scheduler repair
hypothesis: An authentic Ninja scheduler regression can require reconciling static graph state, dynamically loaded outputs, and compiler depfile edges before deciding downstream dirtiness.
why_hard: An output discovered through dyndep may already be referenced in a depfile. Correct scheduling must reconsider its consumer after dynamic dependency discovery while preserving no-op builds.
next_action: Retire the tested snapshot from Sol selection after a valid Terra/high pass.

sources.note: Recorded executable upstream reproducer: a depfile reference to a dyndep output does not trigger the expected downstream rebuild; a public fix exists.
Recorded contract source for depfiles and dynamic dependency behavior.

notes: Actual v1.12.1 scheduler regression reproduced. Two oracle failures were packaging/permission errors, then oracle1/nop0. Terra/high passed in379.766s with a legitimate cross-file graph.cc/graph.h repair and regression coverage; no Sol trial. Public-patch discoverability remains a promotion concern, but the observed trajectory diagnosed locally.
